prompt: LLVM llvm.sqrt negative number behavior vs libm
answer:
`llvm.sqrt` and `libm` `sqrt` differ for negative inputs:

| Input | `llvm.sqrt` | `libm sqrt` |
|---|---|---|
| Negative number less than `-0.0` | Undefined behavior historically; LLVM may produce an undefined value and may optimize assuming this case does not occur | Returns NaN |
| `-0.0` | Defined to return `-0.0` | Returns `-0.0`, like IEEE square root |

The LLVM intrinsic’s negative-input behavior was intended to avoid concerns about `errno` and floating-point environment side effects. In contrast, lowering `llvm.sqrt` to a `libm` call can set `errno`; LLVM discussions specifically identify this as a semantic mismatch.

Sources: [LLVM LangRef change discussion](https://reviews.llvm.org/D28797), [LLVM vectorization discussion](https://reviews.llvm.org/D27618), [LLVM sqrt mapping patch](https://lists.llvm.org/pipermail/cfe-commits/Week-of-Mon-20130909/088596.html).
